scope: Theorem 3.1 (Joint glancing parametrization) of the manuscript “Rigidity of Smooth Billiards with a Continuous Caustic Collar” (preprints/Rigidity-of-Smooth-Billiards-with-a-Continuous-Caustic-Collar-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 147 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0fefc18481d52acb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are s, r1 > 0, with r1 < s, and a real- symmetric holomorphic function U(y, t) on {(y, t) : |ℑy| < 2s, |t| < r1} such that U − y is 2π-periodic in y, U is even in t, U(y, 0) = y, and D1 U(y, t), U(y + t, t)  + D2 U(y − t, t), U(y, t)  = 0 (3.2) for |ℑy| < s, |t| < r1. Here real symmetry means U(ȳ, t̄) = U(y, t). Set Θ(y, t) = ϕ(U(y, t)), p(y, t) = −S1 Θ(y, t), Θ(y + t, t)  . (3.3) On a possibly smaller product neighborhood, both functions are holomorphic, real-symmetric, and even in t. For positive small real t, the billiard map sends the line (Θ(y, t), p(y, t)) to the line (Θ(y + t, t), p(y + t, t)). The variables (y, t2) give analytic coordinates on a full one-sided phase collar. Moreover, dp ∧ dΘ = A(t) dy ∧ dt, A(t) = c 4 t + O(t3 ), (3.4) where A is holomorphic and real on the real axis. In particular t2 is a nondegenerate analytic first integral on that collar.
